scripts.dev:main: npm run build:preload && tsc -p tsconfig.main.json && NODE_ENV=development electron-forge start
scripts.build: npm run build:renderer && npm run build:preload && npm run build:main

//engines: node's floor was raised from the former >=24.0.0 when jsdom 30 landed here (PR #2709): jsdom@30 declares node ^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0, so >=24.0.0 advertised 24.0-24.14 as supported while the test environment was not. This mirrors the same correction made in client/admin (PR #2715). Advisory only — no .npmrc in this repo sets engine-strict — and CI is unaffected either way because setup-node's `node-version: 24` resolves the newest 24.x.
//overrides_security: VALIDATED 2026-08-15 — every entry below was re-checked against the live advisory data (gh api /advisories?ecosystem=npm&affects=<pkg>) and against what each consumer actually declares (npm ls <pkg> --all). GOVERNING PRINCIPLE: every remaining skew in .override-range-baseline.json is UPWARD — a consumer declaring an older range receives a newer, fully patched version. No consumer is held below its declared floor. That property is what the override-range lint (scripts/security/override-range-lint.mjs, #2768) enforces, and two entries below were CORRECTED in this pass because they had quietly stopped satisfying it.  CORRECTED THIS PASS. tar@^7.5.22 replaces a former ^7.5.16, which the lockfile had pinned at 7.5.19 — VULNERABLE to GHSA-r292-9mhp-454m (<= 7.5.20, patched 7.5.21). npm audit graded it moderate, so the HIGH/CRITICAL gate never blocked it: a security override had itself gone stale onto a vulnerable version. Five consumers: ^7.5.4 and ^7.5.7 are satisfied; ^6.0.5, ^6.1.11 and ^6.2.1 are forced up a major. Those three would also be patched on their own line (6.2.1 clears GHSA-f5x3-32g6-xq36, the highest 6.x floor), so the major skew is a deliberate preference for ONE hoisted copy on the newest line, not a security necessity — the ^7 consumers need 7.x regardless. postcss@^8.5.25 replaces ^8.5.18, which the lockfile had pinned at 8.5.23 while vite declares ^8.5.25 — the override was holding vite BELOW its own declared floor. 8.5.23 was patched (GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp floor 8.5.23), so this was a correctness problem rather than a security one; it now resolves 8.5.26 and vite is satisfied.  MINIMATCH + BRACE-EXPANSION — the cap is gone. minimatch@^10.2.6 and brace-expansion@^5.0.9 replace a ^9.0.7 / ^2.1.4 pair. The old minimatch pin was a downgrade CAP: eslint@10 and the @typescript-eslint chain declare ^10.2.2 - ^10.2.5, and capping at 9 forced fifteen consumers down a major. The former rationale warned that brace-expansion 5.x "breaks eslint" — that was true only WHILE minimatch was capped at 9, because minimatch@9 is what calls the 2.x default export 5.x dropped. Lifting both together resolves it, which client/admin had already established (PR #2715) with the note "Do not re-add a minimatch pin below 10". Verified here, not assumed: `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and the full 13,040-test suite all pass on minimatch 10.2.6 + brace-expansion 5.0.9. 10.2.6 sits above every 10.x advisory floor (GHSA-3ppc-4f35-3m26 at 10.2.1; GHSA-7r86-cg39-jmmj and GHSA-23c5-xmqv-rm74 at 10.2.3), and 5.0.9 above every 4.x/5.x floor (GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 at 5.0.9 — note ZERO headroom, it sits exactly on that boundary). Ten consumers declaring ^3.x, ^5.x or ^9.0.3 are still forced up; those ranges are stale upstream metadata, and 10.x is the only line above all four advisory boundaries at once.  LOAD-BEARING — the consumer would be VULNERABLE without the override. ws@^8.21.3 — engine.io-client declares ~8.20.1, which resolves 8.20.1 and is vulnerable to GHSA-96hv-2xvq-fx4p (>= 8.0.0 < 8.21.0). ws is one of exactly THREE runtime-reachable overrides in this block (with js-yaml and socket.io-parser), so this one is not merely a build-time concern. Raised from a former ^8.21.0, which sat exactly on the advisory boundary with no headroom. tmp@^0.2.7 — external-editor declares ^0.0.33, which resolves 0.0.33 and is vulnerable to GHSA-ph9p-34f9-6g65 (< 0.2.6) and GHSA-7c78-jf6q-g5cm (< 0.2.7). 0.2.7 is both the fix and the newest release. A second consumer declares ^0.2.0 and is satisfied. js-yaml@^4.3.1 closes GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj (quadratic CPU consumption in !!omap resolution; 4.x first-patched 4.3.1, 3.x 3.15.1). Runtime-reachable and therefore fixed rather than accepted: electron-updater parses update manifests with it inside the main process, i.e. against remote-fetched content. All six consumers declare ^4.1.0 and are satisfied. ip-address@^10.3.1 closes GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr (leading-zero octets decoded as decimal while resolvers decode octal -> SSRF/trust-boundary bypass; vulnerable <= 10.3.0). fast-uri@^3.1.5 closes GHSA-7p8r-x3mc-p8w7 (host confusion via backslash authority introducer; 3.x first-patched 3.1.5). nanoid@^3.3.17 closes GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 (custom generators loop indefinitely at size zero; transitive via vite -> postcss). socket.io-parser@~4.2.7 closes GHSA-2m8v-j782-fhvr (zero-attachment memory exhaustion; transitive via socket.io-client). TILDE, not caret, and deliberately so: socket.io-client declares ~4.2.4, so a caret would force a future 4.3.x under a client that never declared compatibility with it. This is the wire-format decoder — silent minor drift is a protocol-compatibility risk, not merely a behavioural one.  NOT LOAD-BEARING, kept deliberately at the newest release. shell-quote@^1.10.0 — concurrently declares exactly 1.9.0, and 1.9.0 IS patched (GHSA-395f-4hp3-45gv, floor 1.9.0). The override is therefore not required for security. It is kept because shell-quote has three CRITICAL advisories in its history, the newest release is only one minor above what the consumer pins, and the cost of being one release behind on a shell-argument parser is worse than the cost of the skew. Revisit if it ever forces a major. @tootallnate/once@^3.0.1 — http-proxy-agent declares "2", which resolves 2.0.1, and 2.0.1 IS patched (GHSA-vpq2-c234-7xj6, floor 2.0.1 on the 2.x line). Same reasoning as shell-quote: not required, kept at the newest release. Both advisories on this package are LOW.  DORMANT — present but binding nothing in this lockfile. serialize-javascript@^7.0.3 and rollup@^4.59.0 currently have ZERO consumers here, so they constrain nothing. They are left in place rather than pruned: a former fast-uri override was removed from client/admin on exactly this basis, and that decision was explicitly recorded there as specific to fast-uri and NOT a general instruction to sweep. The npm-audit gate, which resolves live against this lockfile on every CI run, is the control that would catch a reintroduction. @babel/core@^7.29.6 has one consumer declaring ^7.29.0 and is satisfied.  HOW TO RE-VALIDATE (do this, do not trust the text above indefinitely). 1. `npm ls <pkg> --all` for the REAL consumer set — a lockfile scan of `dependencies` missed one of undici's three consumers during #2709. 2. `gh api "/advisories?ecosystem=npm&affects=<pkg>"` and read the per-line first_patched_version for EVERY advisory, not one. Issue #2441 is the founding incident for that rule: a first-patched claim is meaningless without the LINE it applies to. 3. `node scripts/security/override-range-lint.mjs --dir client/desktop` — it fails on any NEW skew and warns on baseline rows that no longer occur. Note that npm itself will never tell you: overriding a declared range is the feature, so there is no warning, no ERESOLVE, and no `invalid` marker from npm ls. Two entries above had silently gone wrong before anyone looked.
